qt: to the Commission Siegbert Frank Droese (ESN) Subject:

A digital catch certificate system for all fishery products entering the EU, known as CATCH, came into force on 10 January 2026. The ambitious system replaced the previous paper-based process and is considered central to EU efforts to tackle illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, help protect marine biodiversity and contribute to the EU’s broader efforts to simplify administrative procedures. Will the Commission please list all persons and organisations (e.g. non-governmental organisations, trade organisations, logistics experts and non-EU exporters) that were consulted in any way during the development of the CATCH system?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.11.2026) The previous paper-based catch certification scheme showed limitations in terms of risk of fraud, burdensome controls for national authorities and uneven import controls across the EU. Member States’ authorities, industry, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and the European Parliament called for a single IT system to manage catch certificates and reduce opportunities for fraudulent imports. Work on CATCH1 started in 2016. Since its first release in 2019, the system has been available to Member States’ authorities and operators for testing and operational use including the possibility for user feedback to the Commission. In 2018, the Commission proposed to amend Council Regulation (EC) 1005/2008 (when revising the Union Fisheries Control System)2 providing, among other, requirements regarding CATCH including its compulsory use by Member State authorities and operators. This proposal was subject to a public stakeholder consultation and feedback3. After its first release in 2019, and most intensively after the adoption of the amended Council Regulation (EC) 1005/20084 by co-legislators in 2023, CATCH has undergone significant further developments. The entire evolution of the system has taken place in consultation primarily with Member States’ authorities. Forthcoming changes to the catch certification scheme, including CATCH-related matters, have been discussed on various occasions with stakeholders in the fisheries sector – industry association and NGOs (through EU Advisory Councils5) and non-EU country authorities.
1 Integrated computerised information management system for the Catch Certification Scheme (Art. 12a of the

Council Regulation (EC) 1005/2008). 2 COM(2018) 368 final. 3 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32023R2842&qid=1791464166490. 4 https://ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say/initiatives/1128-Fisheries-Control-System_en. 5 MAC – Market Advisory Council; LDAC – Long Distance Advisory Council; CCRUP – Outermost regions Advisory Council; Inter-AC – Inter-Advisory Councils.
